title: Dialogic picture book reading as a parent-centered intervention for children with hearing impairmenttere Studiendokumente
summary:
For some children with hearing loss, difficulties in language acquisition persist despite early provision with hearing aids or cochlear implants. In Germany, speech therapy is currently provided mostly as individual therapy directly with the child (child-centered approach). However, research has shown that the language input provided by parents in everyday life is crucial for children’s language development. For this reason, guidelines and experts recommend parent training, especially shared dialogic picture book reading (parent-centered approach).
The DiaLog study is the first in Germany to examine how effective the following two types of therapy are in comparison:

• New parent program DiaLog: In 6 sessions (4 group meetings, including 2 online, plus 2 individual sessions with video feedback and child), parents learn how to actively support their children’s language development while looking at picture books together.

• Conventional child-centered speech therapy: Conducted in a speech therapy practice, once a week with 45-minute individual sessions.

Both therapy formats last three months. If a child is already receiving speech therapy, it will be paused during the study and then continued as usual if further therapy is needed.

interventions.name:
Study Design
Block-randomized, controlled intervention study with two parallel groups to demonstrate the non-inferiority of the parent-centered DiaLog program compared to standard child-centered individual therapy.
A total of 64 parent–child dyads with children using hearing aids or cochlear impla

Study Population
64 parent–child dyads with children using hearing aids or cochlear implants, with at least moderate peripheral hearing loss, aged 2;6 to ≤ 5;2 years, randomized into the control group (standard speech therapy).

Assessment Time Points
Identical to the intervention group (IG).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least moderate, bilateral, permanent hearing loss, present from birth or acquired/manifested within the first 9 months of life
Early audiological intervention (hearing aids [HA] within the first 9 months; cochlear implants [CI] by no later than 19 months)
Spoken-language oriented, monolingual German or multilingual family environment (at least one parent speaks German very well; German is the target language)
No severe intellectual impairment (IQ ≥ 77.5)
At risk for or mild (norm deviation in age-appropriate language tests > -1 SD) or manifest (norm deviation > -1.5 SD) speech and language development disorder (SLD), with at least emerging spoken language (i.e., mean length of utterance of at least 1–1.5 words in the younger age group from 2;6 years, word combinations from 3;0 years, and multi-word utterances from 3;6 years)
Exclusion criteria:
Comorbidities (intellectual disability/IQ < 77.5, autism spectrum disorder, pragmatic-communicative disorders, central speech and language disorders, severe visual impairments/blindness)
Behavioral and developmental difficulties (shared picture book reading not possible or only very limited)
Child’s language development too advanced (better than -1 SD)
Child’s language development too delayed (absent or severely impaired spoken language development)
Insufficient German language skills of both parents for participation
Children indicated for cochlear implantation at study start and with already planned/proposed CI provision within the next 9 months cannot participate
